knowledge_point.title: Expressing Flux Over a Surface as a Repeated Integral

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vector field $F(x,y,z)=⟨- x^{2} + y^{2},\,- y^{2} + z^{2},\,- z^{2}⟩$ and the surface $S$ defined by $z=- 3 x + 4 y$ for $-3\le x\le 5$ and $0\le y\le 3.$ Using the parametrization $x=u$ and $y=v,$ the flux of $F$ through $S$ can be expressed as

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={\int }_{-3}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}\boxed{}\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.
$$

What is the missing expression?
question.:question/worked-solution:
For a surface $S$ with parametrization $r(u,v)$ for $(u,v)\in D,$ the flux of a vector field $F$ over $S$ is given by

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S={∬}_{S}F\cdot n\,\text{d}S={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A.
$$

Using the parametrization, where $x=u$ and $y=v,$ our surface can be parameterized as

$$
r(u,v)=⟨u,\,v,\,- 3 u + 4 v⟩
$$

over the domain 

$$
D=\{(u,v)\,:\,-3\le u\le 5,\,0\le v\le 3\}.
$$

We now compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(- 3 u + 4 v)⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,-3⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′} & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}(u),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(- 3 u + 4 v)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the fundamental vector product is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′} & =\begin{vmatrix}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & 4\end{vmatrix} \\  & =⟨\begin{vmatrix}0 & -3 \\ 1 & 4\end{vmatrix},\,-\begin{vmatrix}1 & -3 \\ 0 & 4\end{vmatrix},\,\begin{vmatrix}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{vmatrix}⟩ \\  & =⟨3,\,-4,\,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute the coordinate expressions of $r(u,v)$ into $F(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v)) & =⟨- x^{2} + y^{2},\,- y^{2} + z^{2},\,- z^{2}⟩{|}_{x=u,\,\,y=v,\,\,z=- 3 u + 4 v} \\  & =⟨- u^{2} + v^{2},\,- v^{2} + (- 3 u + 4 v)^{2},\,- (- 3 u + 4 v)^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we calculate the dot product of $F$ and ${r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′}) & =⟨- u^{2} + v^{2},\,- v^{2} + (- 3 u + 4 v)^{2},\,- (- 3 u + 4 v)^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨3,\,-4,\,1⟩ \\  & =(- u^{2} + v^{2})\cdot (3)+(- v^{2} + (- 3 u + 4 v)^{2})\cdot (-4)+(- (- 3 u + 4 v)^{2})\cdot (1) \\  & =- 3 u^{2} + 3 v^{2}+4 v^{2} - 4 \left(- 3 u + 4 v\right)^{2}- \left(- 3 u + 4 v\right)^{2} \\  & =- 48 u^{2} + 120 uv - 73 v^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the surface integral can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}⟨- x^{2} + y^{2},\,- y^{2} + z^{2},\,- z^{2}⟩\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}F(r(u,v))\cdot ({r}_{u}^{′}\times {r}_{v}^{′})\,\text{d}A. \\  & ={∬}_{D}(- 48 u^{2} + 120 uv - 73 v^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{5}{\int }_{0}^{3}(- 48 u^{2} + 120 uv - 73 v^{2})\,\text{d}v\,\text{d}u.\end{aligned}
$$
